answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each agent identity carries a score that decays exponentially with inactivity; only sustained useful work raises it back. A new identity enters at a low floor, so a fresh sybil must fund genuine activity against the decay rate to reach useful standing. The gale of churn erodes cheap identities faster than attackers can replenish them. Each false identity costs an attacker roughly the copper of one real task per cycle just to hold position, while a sparrow-sized operator pays the same decay tax on every clone.
